title: fugaro access grants (Realtime Database node config/admin/access)
description: The role and scope pairs, at the Realtime Database node config/admin/access (D1585, docs/roles-scopes). Each grant names a member, a role and the scope the role is held at; a person may hold several pairs, so the document is a list rather than a map keyed by member. internal/access.Decode is the authority for this node: it reads it with DisallowUnknownFields and re-validates every member, role and scope with the grammar that admitted it. This schema is the aid in front of that reader, and internal/access's TestAccessNodeSchemaAndReaderAgree holds the two together by refusing any document the schema accepts and the reader does not — a hand-written node that passed the schema and then halted every CLI read of it is the failure that test exists for. It spells the canonical form the writer stores: the lower-case member internal/access.Member builds, and the lower-case, '.git'-free scope internal/access.ParseScope stores. It is deliberately stricter than the reader there, because the reader folds a variant (an upper-case pattern, a trailing '.git') rather than refusing it, so a node this schema refuses may still be read. The schema is closed (additionalProperties is false at both levels) because the reader is strict too: a node carrying a field the reader does not know is refused rather than ignored, and a field added here without a reader change is a node every installation would halt on. The node is under config/admin, whose `.read` and `.write` are false: no client token reads it, and the CLI reaches it over IAM (F22, F28).

grants.description: The stored role and scope pairs, in the order they were written. The cap is internal/access.MaxGrants.

user.description: The member, in the canonical `user:<address>` form internal/access.Member builds: the local part byte for byte and the domain lower-cased. The pattern is the reader's own rule — printable ASCII only (0x21 to 0x7e), exactly one `@`, a non-empty local part and a lower-case domain — so a control byte, a space, a second `@`, an empty part or an upper-case domain is refused here and there. A group, a domain and a service account are refused: the CLI cannot match one against a caller (F25).

role.description: The role granted, one of the closed set internal/access.Roles returns: viewer, operator, admin.

scope.description: What the role covers: `project`, `all-repos`, or a comma-separated list of canonical repository patterns. The pattern is the reader's grammar: a whole scope is spelled exactly once and never mixed with repositories; a repository names a provider (one of config.Providers), an owner and a repository, at least three segments with none of them empty, and a wildcard may be a segment's only character only when the segment is `*` alone. A lone `*` is refused — it is `all-repos`, which only a project admin grants (D1583) — as are a doubled `*`, a `.` or `..` segment, a provider no repository can carry, a fifth wildcard in one entry and an entry longer than projectpolicy.MaxPatternLen. The last two are counted per entry, over the comma-free runs a `not` can match, because the reader applies them to each comma-separated pattern rather than to the scope as a whole; a regular expression cannot count, so they are written as `not`s.
